newsitem.title: ITALY: Greenshoe option used in Italy's ENI sale.
newsitem.headline: Greenshoe option used in Italy's ENI sale.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said it had fully used an over-allotment, or "greenshoe," option placed on the second tranche sale of shares in energy group ENI.
A total 165 million additional shares were put in the greenshoe reserve for institutional investors on top of the 400 million shares they were originally allocated.
The Treasury, whose stake in ENI now falls to 69 percent, said in a statement the sale had been a success.

The Treasury raised 7.7 trillion lire from the sale of some 14 percent of its stake in the group last month. With all the greenshoe sold, the Treasury will raise a total gross around 9.0 trillion lire from the second tranche sale.
It originally planned to sell just 700 million shares but with the greenshoe option, the Treasury has sold a total 1.265 billion shares.
An initial 15 percent of ENI was placed on the market in November last year.
ENI shares closed down 0.28 percent at 7,903 lire on Wednesday on a sharply weaker Milan stock market.
